subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Explain the extraction of zinc from zinc blende.

verification.note: Unit 6 (Metallurgy) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book p.81, which prints the question and a model answer. The 1+1+1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. EQUATIONS CHECKED: both printed equations balance as printed — 2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂ (Zn 2=2, S 2=2, O 6=6) and ZnO + C → Zn + CO (Zn 1=1, O 1=1, C 1=1). BOOK NUMBERING ERROR (book p.81, SAQ 4): the printed answer has FIVE stages but numbers them i, ii, iii, iv, iv — "iv)" appears twice, so reduction and electrolytic refining are both printed as stage four. The stages are numbered 1 to 5 on this card. BOOK TYPOS: the question is printed "Explain the extration of zinc from zinc blende" (extration for extraction) and the acid is printed "dill H₂SO₄" for dilute H₂SO₄; both are written correctly here. BOOK NOTATION: the book writes the ion as Zn⁺²; the number is written before the sign here, Zn²⁺. BOOK GAP: the book does not say that zinc distils over as a vapour, which is why the retort is used at all; zinc boils at 1180 K, well below the 1673 K of the reduction, and that is added.

steps.label: Concentration
lines: 1) Crushing: the ore is crushed to a fine
steps.why: Froth flotation is chosen because zinc blende is a sulphide, and froth flotation is the concentration method that suits a sulphide ore. Crushing has to come first, because flotation acts on the surface of the particles and needs them fine.
common_mistakes: Concentrating zinc blende by leaching. Leaching is used for bauxite; a sulphide ore is concentrated by froth flotation.
Leaving out the crushing. Flotation needs a fine powder to work at all.
steps.memory_tip: A sulphide ore means froth flotation, and crushing comes first.
steps.margin_note: Naming the method and saying why it suits a sulphide ore earns this mark.

steps.label: Roasting

lines.text: heated in a regular supply of air at
about 1200 K to give zinc oxide.

lines: The SO₂ given off is used to make
steps.why: Zinc sulphide cannot be reduced by carbon directly, so it is first turned into the oxide. Roasting does that and sends the sulphur off as SO₂ in the same step.
common_mistakes: Trying to reduce ZnS with carbon straight away. The sulphide has to be roasted to ZnO first.
Writing ZnS + O₂ → ZnO + SO₂. The equation needs 2ZnS and 3O₂ to balance.
steps.margin_note: The balanced roasting equation is the mark. The temperature is worth adding beside it.

lines: Zinc boils at 1180 K, so it distils over
as a vapour and is condensed. The metal
steps.why: Carbon is the reducing agent because above 983 K it lies below CO on the Ellingham diagram, so it removes oxygen more readily than CO does at furnace temperature. The furnace runs well above the boiling point of zinc, so the metal leaves as a vapour and is condensed away from the charge.
common_mistakes: Using CO as the reducing agent. At 1673 K carbon is the better reducing agent for ZnO.
Writing ZnO + C → Zn + CO₂. One carbon atom takes the one oxygen atom of ZnO, so the product is CO.
steps.memory_tip: Coke at 1673 K, and the zinc comes off as a vapour.
steps.margin_note: The reduction equation with its temperature carries this mark.

steps.label: Refining
lines: 5) Refining: the zinc is purified by
steps.why: The impure metal is made the anode so that it dissolves, and the pure zinc is deposited on the cathode. The ion is written Zn²⁺, with the number before the sign.
common_mistakes: Making the pure zinc the anode. The impure metal must be the anode.
Writing the ion as Zn⁺². The number comes first and the sign after it: Zn²⁺.
steps.memory_tip: Impure zinc dissolves at the anode and pure zinc is deposited at the cathode.
steps.margin_note: Both electrode equations and the electrolyte finish this answer.

insider_note: Five stages but four marks: crushing and concentration share one. The two equations, roasting and reduction, are what the examiner looks for first.
